content.text: {"title":"A Request That Never Touches the Network","premise":"A caller wants to exercise a plain Python WSGI application through the real httpx client — same headers, same cookie jar, same response model — but with no socket, no DNS and no TLS anywhere in the path. The input is modest: the string \"/\" and one custom header, handed to `client.get()`. Everything interesting is what the client does to that input on the way down, and what it guarantees about what comes back up. The reader following it is the person who has to sign off on that stack: which defaults are in force, where a failure would surface, and what the transport boundary does and does not promise.","chapters":[{"n":1,"title":"The world it enters: a client wired to a function, not a socket","trace_lines":[2,75],"data_in":"app=<function app>, transport=httpx.WSGITransport(app=app), base_url='http://testserver', everything else left at defaults","data_out":"An OPENED Client whose _transport is the WSGITransport, _mounts == {}, base_url == URL('http://testserver') (raw_path b'/'), default headers Accept/Accept-Encoding/Connection/User-Agent, timeout Timeout(5.0), follow_redirects=False","code":["httpx/_transports/wsgi.py:77-89","httpx/_client.py:639-716","httpx/_client.py:188-221","httpx/_client.py:234-251","httpx/_client.py:298-316","httpx/_client.py:1275-1291"],"inputs":["app callable","base_url='http://testserver'","transport=WSGITransport(app=app)"],"characters":["WSGITransport","Client","BaseClient","Headers","Timeout","Limits","ClientState"],"facts":["`allow_env_proxies = trust_env and transport is None`, so passing an explicit transport disables environment-variable proxying even though trust_env stays True; Does it touch the request, and how many times can it make the client re-send?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":6,"title":"The auth generator: one yield, one pass","trace_lines":[256,260],"data_in":"<Request('GET','http://testserver/')> plus the bare Auth instance, history=[]","data_out":"the same Request object, handed onward to the redirect layer","code":["httpx/_client.py:930-962","httpx/_auth.py:22-85","httpx/_client.py:573-582"],"inputs":["the Request and Auth from chapter 5"],"characters":["Client._send_handling_auth","Auth.sync_auth_flow","Auth.auth_flow"],"facts":["`sync_auth_flow` only pre-reads the request body when the scheme sets `requires_request_body = True`; the base Auth does not, so nothing is read here (_auth.py:71-75).","The flow is driven as a generator: `next(flow)` gives the request to send, and each response is pushed back in with `flow.send(response)`; StopIteration ends the loop and returns the last response (_client.py:937-951).","Every intermediate response in a multi-step auth flow is fully read into memory and appended to `history` before the next request goes out — so a custom auth scheme implies buffering (_client.py:953-956).","`auth_flow.close()` runs in a `finally`, so a generator-based auth scheme is always finalised even when the caller's request raises (_client.py:961-962).","Answering replay: `_redirect_stream` hands the *same* `request.stream` to the follow-up request; a `ByteStream` (the case here, and for bytes/str/json bodies) replays fine, whereas a generator body raises `StreamConsumed` on the second pass (_client.py:573-582, _content.py:50-53)."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q4.1","answer":"Yes for this request. A generator/file-iterator body would instead raise `StreamConsumed` on the second send — which is exactly why eagerly-read ByteStream bodies are the safe default."},{"id":"q5.1","answer":"It does nothing to the request: `Auth.auth_flow` yields it unchanged and ends. A custom header like `X-Custom` is *not* stripped — it follows the redirect to the new origin."},{"id":"q6.1","answer":"Hooks run inside the loop's try block; an exception from a request or response hook triggers `response.close()` and is re-raised, and `send()`'s own handler closes again if needed. A plain list has none, so it is a no-op here — but a generator-based or file-backed WSGI app does get closed."},{"id":"q9.1","answer":"On that same close. `BoundSyncStream.close` computes `time.perf_counter() - start` and assigns `response.elapsed` before delegating to the underlying stream, so for a non-streaming request `elapsed` is set as soon as `send()`'s `response.read()` finishes.
